title: Help page reachable from the sidebar and renders its header
objective: Help copy: page header "Help / How to work with the asset register." -- verify the documentation entry point exists and is reachable from primary navigation.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/.
Click the "Help" item in the left sidebar navigation.
Inspect the URL, the H1 and the description paragraph.
expected_result: URL is /help; H1 reads "Help"; the description reads "How to work with the asset register."; the sidebar "Help" item is rendered in the current/active state.

title: Help page reachable from the top-bar help icon
objective: Help copy: the whole page -- verify the second documented entry point (top-bar icon, aria-label "Help") reaches the same page.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets at a viewport of 1440x900.
Activate the top-bar control with accessible name "Help".
expected_result: Navigation lands on /help with the H1 "Help" visible; no full page reload is required.

title: Help page exposes three labelled sections
objective: Help copy: section headings "Finding assets", "Registering and editing assets", "Access and visibility" -- verify all three render and are programmatically labelled.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/help.
Capture the accessibility snapshot of the main region.
For each section element, read its aria-labelledby target and the referenced H2 text.
expected_result: Exactly three sections are present, in order, with H2 text "Finding assets", "Registering and editing assets", "Access and visibility"; each section's aria-labelledby resolves to its own H2 (help-search / help-register / help-access).

title: Help body copy matches the shipped strings verbatim (documentation drift guard)
objective: Help copy: all eight bullets and the Access paragraph -- verify the rendered text still matches the strings this suite is written against, so a copy change forces a test review.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Expected strings are the eight <li> items and the Access paragraph in frontend/app/pages/help.vue.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/help.
Extract the text content of every list item in the three sections plus the Access-and-visibility paragraph.
Compare against the expected strings recorded with this case.
expected_result: Every rendered string matches its expected value exactly (whitespace-normalised). Any mismatch fails this case and requires the affected TC-HELP-* cases to be re-reviewed before they are executed.

title: Help page passes an automated accessibility scan
objective: Help copy: the whole page -- documentation must itself be accessible; verify no serious or critical axe violations and a correct heading hierarchy.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/help.
Run an axe scan scoped to the document.
Read back the heading levels in DOM order.
expected_result: Zero violations at serious or critical impact; headings are h1 followed by three h2s with no skipped levels; every list is a real ul/li.

title: Help page is readable at mobile width with no horizontal scroll
objective: Help copy: the whole page -- verify the guidance is usable on the mobile breakpoint the app claims to support.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Resize the viewport to 375x812.
Open http://localhost:3000/help.
Compare document.scrollWidth with window.innerWidth and read the visible text.
expected_result: scrollWidth is not greater than innerWidth (no horizontal scrolling); all three section headings and their body copy remain visible and legible; no text is clipped.

title: Global search box is present in the top bar with an accessible label
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar to search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the control exists and its accessible name names those fields.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/ at 1440x900.
Locate the combobox in the top bar and read its accessible name and ARIA attributes.
expected_result: A role="combobox" input is present in the top bar with accessible name "Search assets by tag, serial, name, model, custodian, or location", aria-autocomplete="list" and aria-expanded="false" while closed.

title: Single-character input does not open the suggestion list
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify the minimum-length gate so the listbox does not flicker open on the first keystroke.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/.
Type a single character into the global search box and wait 1 second.
expected_result: No listbox is rendered; aria-expanded stays "false"; no search request is issued.

title: Global search finds an asset by asset tag
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag..." -- verify the tag field is searchable from the top bar.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Tag of a seeded asset, read from the first row of /assets.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and copy the tag shown in the first table row.
Open http://localhost:3000/.
Type the tag into the global search box and wait for suggestions.
expected_result: The suggestion listbox opens and contains an option whose monospace tag text equals the searched tag, together with that asset's name.

title: Exact tag match is ranked first among multiple hits
objective: Help copy: "Exact tag matches appear first." -- verify ranking, not just retrieval.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: A tag value that is also a strict prefix of at least one other asset tag (for example AST-0001 alongside AST-00010); confirm via GET /api/v1/assets?q=<prefix> before running.
steps: Identify a tag T that is both an exact tag of one asset and a prefix of other tags.
Open http://localhost:3000/ and type T into the global search box.
Wait for the listbox and read the options in order.
expected_result: The first option in the listbox is the asset whose tag equals T exactly; partial/prefix matches follow it. Ranking is stable across repeated runs.

title: Global search finds an asset by serial number
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the serial number field is actually searchable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Search term: serial_number of a seeded asset (read from the asset detail page or the list API first).
steps: Read a known serial number value from a seeded asset.
Open http://localhost:3000/ and type that value into the global search box.
Wait for the suggestion listbox.
expected_result: The listbox opens with at least one option, and the expected asset (matched by tag) is among the returned options -- proving serial number participates in the search index.

title: Global search finds an asset by name
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the name field is actually searchable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Search term: a distinctive word from a seeded asset name (read from the asset detail page or the list API first).
steps: Read a known name value from a seeded asset.
Open http://localhost:3000/ and type that value into the global search box.
Wait for the suggestion listbox.
expected_result: The listbox opens with at least one option, and the expected asset (matched by tag) is among the returned options -- proving name participates in the search index.

title: Global search finds an asset by model
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the model field is actually searchable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).

steps: Read a known model value from a seeded asset.

Wait for the suggestion listbox.
expected_result: The listbox opens with at least one option, and the expected asset (matched by tag) is among the returned options -- proving model participates in the search index.

title: Global search finds an asset by custodian
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the custodian field is actually searchable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).

steps: Read a known custodian value from a seeded asset.
Open http://localhost:3000/ and type that value into the global search box.
Wait for the suggestion listbox.
expected_result: The listbox opens with at least one option, and the expected asset (matched by tag) is among the returned options -- proving custodian participates in the search index.

title: Global search finds an asset by location
objective: Help copy: "...search by asset tag, serial number, name, model, custodian, or location." -- verify the location field is actually searchable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Search term: name of a seeded location (read from the asset detail page or the list API first).
steps: Read a known location value from a seeded asset.
Open http://localhost:3000/ and type that value into the global search box.
Wait for the suggestion listbox.
expected_result: The listbox opens with at least one option, and the expected asset (matched by tag) is among the returned options -- proving location participates in the search index.

title: Choosing a suggestion opens that asset's detail page
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify the suggestion is actionable, not decorative.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/ and search for a known tag.
Click the first suggestion.
expected_result: Navigation lands on /assets/<uuid> for the chosen asset; the detail heading shows that asset's name; the search box is cleared and the listbox closed.

title: Pressing Enter without a highlighted suggestion runs a full search
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify the fallback path from the quick search into the full asset register.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/.
Type a multi-result term into the global search box.
Press Enter without arrowing into the suggestion list.
expected_result: Navigation lands on /assets?q=<term>; the register shows the matching results and a chip labelled Search: "<term>".

title: Suggestion list is fully keyboard navigable
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify keyboard parity with the mouse path (WCAG 2.1.1).
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: A term returning at least two suggestions.
steps: Focus the global search box using Tab only.
Type a term returning multiple suggestions.
Press ArrowDown twice, then ArrowUp once, reading aria-activedescendant each time.
Press Enter.
Return to the search box, retype the term, and press Escape.
expected_result: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move aria-activedescendant through the options and wrap at the ends; the highlighted option has aria-selected="true"; Enter opens that asset; Escape closes the listbox and leaves focus in the input.

title: Search with no matches shows the documented empty message
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify the no-result state is explicit rather than an empty dropdown.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/.
Type a term that cannot match any asset and wait for the request to settle.
expected_result: The dropdown opens showing "No assets match this search." and no options; no error toast is raised.

title: Search result count is announced to assistive technology
objective: Help copy: "Use the global search in the top bar..." -- verify screen-reader users learn the outcome of a search.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Query returning a known number of results.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/ and search for a term with matches.
Read the text of the role="status" region next to the search box.
Repeat with a term that has no matches.
expected_result: The status region reads "N result(s) available." for matches and "No assets match this search." for none; it is sr-only (not visually rendered) and is updated, not duplicated.

title: Each documented filter dimension narrows the register
objective: Help copy: "On the asset register, combine filters (status, condition, category, department, location)." -- verify all five dimensions exist and filter.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: One valid value per dimension, taken from the select options themselves.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets at 1440x900 and record the baseline result count.
For each of status, condition, category, department and location: select a value, wait for the list to settle, record the count, then clear it again.
expected_result: All five controls are present and labelled; each selection produces a result count less than or equal to the baseline and a URL query parameter of the same name; clearing it restores the baseline count.

title: Filters combine (AND), not replace
objective: Help copy: "combine filters (status, condition, category, department, location)" -- verify combined filters intersect.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Two dimensions with values that individually match rows.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets.
Apply filter A and record count(A).
Without clearing A, apply filter B and record count(A+B).
Inspect the URL query string.
expected_result: count(A+B) is less than or equal to both count(A) and count(B); the URL carries both parameters; every visible row satisfies both filters.

title: Active filters render as labelled chips
objective: Help copy: "Active filters appear as removable chips..." -- verify each active dimension produces one chip with a human-readable label.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and apply a status and a category filter.
Read the contents of the "Active filters" group.
expected_result: One chip per active dimension, labelled "Status: <label>" and "Category: <name>" using the reference-data display names (not raw UUIDs); a free-text search renders as Search: "<term>"; each chip has a remove button named "Remove filter <label>".

title: Removing a chip clears only that filter
objective: Help copy: "Active filters appear as removable chips..." -- verify "removable" and that removal is surgical.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and apply two filters.
Activate the remove button on the first chip.
Inspect the remaining chips, the URL and the result count.
expected_result: Only the removed dimension disappears from the chips and from the URL; the other filter stays applied and its chip remains; the result count widens to the single-filter count.

title: "Clear all" resets every filter and the URL
objective: Help copy: "Active filters appear as removable chips and the URL stays shareable." -- verify the bulk reset returns to a clean, shareable base URL.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Three filters plus a search term applied.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and apply three filters plus a text search.
Activate "Clear all".
expected_result: All chips disappear; the URL returns to /assets with no query string; the result count returns to the unfiltered total.

title: Filtered URL is shareable and restores identical state
objective: Help copy: "...and the URL stays shareable." -- verify the strongest claim on the page: a copied URL reproduces the same view for the recipient.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets, apply two filters, change the sort, and go to page 2.
Copy the full URL and record the chips, sort indicator and result count.
Open the copied URL in a new browser tab (fresh page load, same session).
expected_result: The freshly loaded page shows the same chips, the same sort column and direction, the same page number and the same result count -- no state is held only in memory.

title: Changing a filter resets pagination to page 1
objective: Help copy: "combine filters..." -- verify a narrowed result set cannot strand the user on an out-of-range page.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: A filter that reduces the result set below one page.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and navigate to page 3.
Apply a filter that reduces the total below one page of results.
expected_result: The URL drops the page parameter (page 1); results are shown rather than an empty page; pagination controls reflect the new total.

title: Register text filter debounces into the q parameter
objective: Help copy: "On the asset register, combine filters..." -- verify the in-page text filter behaves as a filter dimension.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Term: a distinctive substring of a seeded asset name.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets.
Type a term into the "Filter by tag, serial, name..." box and wait ~500ms.
expected_result: Exactly one list request is issued after typing stops; the URL gains q=<term>; a Search: "<term>" chip appears; results narrow accordingly.

title: Over-filtered register shows a recoverable empty state
objective: Help copy: "combine filters..." -- verify a dead-end combination offers a way out.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: A filter combination guaranteed to match nothing.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and apply a combination that matches no assets.
Read the empty state, then activate "Clear all filters".
expected_result: The empty state reads "No assets match your filters" with guidance to broaden the search; the "Clear all filters" button restores the unfiltered list.

title: Mobile filter drawer exposes the active filter count
objective: Help copy: "combine filters..." -- verify filters remain reachable and their state visible below the lg breakpoint.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Resize the viewport to 375x812 and open http://localhost:3000/assets.
Apply two filters via the Filters drawer, then close it.
Read the Filters button's badge and accessible name.
expected_result: The Filters button shows a badge reading "2" and an accessible name of "Open filters, 2 active"; the chips remain visible; the drawer applies and clears filters correctly.

title: Save the current filter combination as a saved view
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." -- verify the primary save path.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and apply at least two filters.
Activate "Save current view", enter a unique name, and activate "Save view".
Inspect the saved-view select.
expected_result: The name form closes; the new view appears as an option in the Saved view select and is the selected option; a "Delete view" button becomes available.

title: Applying a saved view restores its filters and results
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." -- verify the saved combination is actually replayable.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and clear all filters (URL is bare /assets).
Select the saved view from the Saved view select.
expected_result: The URL is rewritten with the saved view's query parameters; the same chips reappear; the result count matches the count recorded when the view was saved.

title: Deleting a saved view removes it from the list
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." -- verify the lifecycle closes cleanly (also the teardown for this suite).
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and select the saved view.
Activate "Delete view".
Reload the page and reopen the select.
expected_result: The view is gone from the select, the selection returns to "None", the "Delete view" button disappears, and the removal survives a reload.

title: A saved view cannot be created without a name
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." -- verify the guard against unnamed views.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and activate "Save current view".
Leave the name empty, then enter only spaces.
expected_result: The "Save view" button stays disabled in both cases; pressing Enter in the name field does not create a view; no request is sent.

title: Saved views persist across reload and re-authentication
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." -- verify views are server-side, not per-tab state.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: A saved view created earlier in the run.
steps: Create a saved view, then reload the page and confirm it is listed.
Sign out, sign back in as the same user, and open /assets.
expected_result: The saved view is present in the select after both the reload and the re-login, with the same name and the same stored filter configuration.

title: A saved view is not visible to a different user
objective: Help copy: "Save frequently used filter combinations as a saved view." combined with "What you can see and do depends on your role and organizational scope." -- verify owner isolation.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: An admin-owned view created in TC-HELP-40; employee credentials.
steps: As admin, create a uniquely named saved view.
Sign out and sign in as `employee`.
Open http://localhost:3000/assets and open the Saved view select.
expected_result: The admin's view is absent from the employee's select (unless explicitly shared, which is labelled "(shared)"); no request exposes another user's view configuration.

title: "New asset" is reachable from the asset register
objective: Help copy: "Choose New asset from the register or top bar." -- verify the first documented entry point.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets.
Activate the "New asset" action in the page header.
expected_result: Navigation lands on /assets/new with the create form rendered and the "Save asset" button present.

title: "New asset" is reachable from the top bar
objective: Help copy: "Choose New asset from the register or top bar." -- verify the second documented entry point.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: Viewport 1440x900 (the top-bar action is sm and up).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/ at 1440x900.
Activate the "New asset" link in the top bar.
expected_result: Navigation lands on /assets/new with the create form rendered.

title: Required fields are marked with an asterisk and explained
objective: Help copy: "Required fields are marked with an asterisk." -- verify the marking exists and is explained in text, not colour alone.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new.
Read the legend above the form and inspect the Asset name and Category fields.
expected_result: The legend reads "Fields marked * are required."; Asset name and Category show the asterisk and carry the required attribute; the asterisk itself is aria-hidden so it is not read as punctuation; optional fields carry no asterisk.

title: Submitting with required fields empty shows field errors and keeps the user on the form
objective: Help copy: "Required fields are marked with an asterisk." -- verify the marking is enforced.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new.
Activate "Save asset" without filling anything in.
expected_result: An error summary with role="alert" receives focus and lists the failing fields; inline messages read "Enter an asset name." and "Select a category."; the offending inputs get aria-invalid="true"; the URL stays /assets/new and no asset is created.

title: Leaving the asset tag blank generates a tag automatically
objective: Help copy: "Leave the asset tag blank to have one generated automatically." -- verify the generated tag is produced and surfaced.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: name: "QA Help Autotag <timestamp>", category: first option, tag: left empty.
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new.
Confirm the Asset tag hint reads "Leave blank to have a tag generated automatically."
Fill in only Asset name and Category, leaving Asset tag empty.
Activate "Save asset" (and "Save asset anyway" if a duplicate panel appears).
expected_result: The asset is created and the browser lands on /assets/<uuid>; a non-empty tag is shown on the detail page and echoed in the success toast; the tag follows the configured tag format and is unique.

title: An explicitly entered asset tag is used as typed
objective: Help copy: "Leave the asset tag blank to have one generated automatically." -- verify the converse: a supplied tag is honoured, not overwritten.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new.
Enter a unique tag along with Asset name and Category.
Save the asset.
expected_result: The created asset's tag on the detail page is exactly the value entered; no generated tag replaces it.

title: Possible duplicates are reported before the first save
objective: Help copy: "Before saving, the app warns you about possible duplicates..." -- verify the pre-check fires and blocks the first save attempt.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: serial_number / manufacturer / model copied from an existing seeded asset.
steps: Read the serial number, manufacturer and model of an existing asset.
Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new and enter a new name, a category, and those same identity values.
Activate "Save asset".
expected_result: A warning panel titled "Possible duplicate assets" appears and receives focus; the asset is NOT created by this first click (verify no navigation and no new record via the list afterwards).

title: Submit label changes to "Save asset anyway" after a duplicate warning
objective: Help copy: "...review them, then save anyway if the asset is genuinely new." -- verify the documented affordance appears verbatim.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Trigger the duplicate warning as in TC-HELP-56.
Read the submit button label and the helper text under the panel.
expected_result: The submit button now reads "Save asset anyway"; the helper text reads "If none of these are the same physical asset, choose “Save asset anyway” to continue."

title: Duplicate panel lists reviewable candidates
objective: Help copy: "...the app warns you about possible duplicates -- review them..." -- verify the candidates are inspectable, which is what makes review possible.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Trigger the duplicate warning as in TC-HELP-56.
Inspect each candidate entry in the panel.
Activate a candidate's "Review" link in a new tab.
expected_result: Each candidate shows its tag (as a link), its name and its match reasons; the Review link opens /assets/<uuid> for that candidate; the create form retains its entered values.

title: "Save asset anyway" completes the registration
objective: Help copy: "...then save anyway if the asset is genuinely new." -- verify the override actually saves.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Trigger the duplicate warning as in TC-HELP-56.
Activate "Save asset anyway".
expected_result: The asset is created, the browser lands on /assets/<uuid>, a success toast names the new tag, and the new asset appears in the register.

title: Editing identity fields re-arms the duplicate pre-check
objective: Help copy: "Before saving, the app warns you about possible duplicates..." -- verify the acknowledgement does not persist after the identity data changes.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Trigger the duplicate warning as in TC-HELP-56.
Change the serial number to a new unique value.
Read the submit button label and check whether the panel is still shown.
expected_result: The duplicate panel is cleared and the submit label reverts to "Save asset"; the next save runs a fresh duplicate pre-check against the new values.

title: Leaving a dirty create form asks for confirmation
objective: Help copy: "Choose New asset..." -- verify entered work is not silently lost, which the registration guidance implicitly relies on.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets/new and fill in the Asset name only.
Attempt to navigate to /assets via the sidebar.
expected_result: Navigation is intercepted and a confirmation dialog is shown; cancelling keeps the form and its values; confirming leaves the page.

title: Edit form is prefilled with the current asset values
objective: Help copy: "If someone else edits the same asset while you work..." -- baseline: verify the edit form loads the current version before concurrency is exercised.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Open http://localhost:3000/assets and open the first asset.
Open its Edit page.
Compare the form values with the detail page values.
expected_result: The heading reads "Edit asset"; name, category, status, condition, department, location and identity fields match the detail page; the submit button reads "Save changes".

title: A concurrent edit produces the documented conflict prompt
objective: Help copy: "If someone else edits the same asset while you work, you will be asked to reload the latest version before saving again." -- verify the core promise.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: One asset UUID; a second update applied out-of-band via PATCH /api/v1/assets/<uuid> with the current version and If-Match header (pattern proven in frontend/tests/e2e/assets.spec.ts).
steps: Open the edit page for an asset and leave it open.
Apply a change to the same asset out-of-band (second session or API call).
Back in the open form, modify the description and activate "Save changes".
expected_result: A warning alert titled "This asset was changed by someone else" is shown and focused, with a message about reloading; a "Reload latest data" button is present; the stale save is rejected (HTTP 409 VERSION_CONFLICT) and the other user's change is not overwritten.

title: "Reload latest data" restores the current version into the form
objective: Help copy: "...you will be asked to reload the latest version before saving again." -- verify the offered remedy works.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: Reach the conflict state described in TC-HELP-66.
Activate "Reload latest data".
expected_result: The form remounts showing the other user's saved values (including the concurrent change); the conflict alert is gone; the stale local edit is discarded rather than silently kept.

title: Re-applying the edit after reloading saves successfully
objective: Help copy: "...before saving again." -- verify the user can complete their work after resolving the conflict.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
steps: After reloading the latest data, re-apply the intended change.
Activate "Save changes".
expected_result: The save succeeds with a success toast; the detail page shows both the concurrent change and the re-applied change; the asset version has incremented; the history records both updates.

title: Client-side field validation on the edit form
objective: Help copy: "Registering and editing assets" -- verify edit-time validation behaves like create-time validation.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: warranty_start later than warranty_end; purchase price "12.345".
steps: Open the edit page for an asset (as a role that can see financial fields).
Set a warranty end date earlier than the warranty start date and save.
Correct the dates, enter an invalid purchase price, and save again.
expected_result: "Warranty end must be on or after the start date." and "Enter a valid amount, for example 1299.99." are shown inline against the right fields; the error summary receives focus; no request is sent for either invalid state.

title: employee does not see asset-creation actions
objective: Help copy: "What you can see and do depends on your role and organizational scope." -- verify a low-privilege role loses the create affordances.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
steps: Sign in as `employee` and open http://localhost:3000/assets at 1440x900.
Look for a "New asset" action in the page header and in the top bar.
expected_result: No "New asset" control exists in either location; the register itself still renders within the user's scope.

title: Financial fields are hidden from employee
objective: Help copy: "Financial fields are restricted to authorized roles." -- verify the field-level restriction on the read path.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
test_data: An asset with a purchase price set.
steps: Sign in as `employee` and open an asset detail page.
Search the page for purchase price, purchase date and any currency amounts.
Inspect the JSON of the underlying GET /api/v1/assets/<uuid> response.
expected_result: No financial section or purchase amount is rendered, and the API response itself omits the restricted fields -- the value is never delivered to the client, not merely hidden by CSS.

title: Hidden actions are also refused server-side for employee
objective: Help copy: "If a page or action is hidden, the backend enforces the same restriction." -- verify the claim by bypassing the UI.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
steps: Sign in as `employee` and navigate directly to http://localhost:3000/assets/new.
Independently POST a valid asset payload to /api/v1/assets with the employee session and CSRF token.
expected_result: The UI route does not yield a usable create form (403 Access denied or redirect), and the direct API call returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with no asset created -- proving the hidden action is a real boundary.

title: auditor sees financial data but no write actions
objective: Help copy: "Financial fields are restricted to authorized roles." -- verify the positive half of the finance rule alongside read-only scope.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `auditor`.
test_data: An asset with a purchase price set.
steps: Sign in as `auditor` and open an asset detail page.
Check for financial fields, and for Edit / New asset actions.
expected_result: Financial fields (purchase price, purchase date) are visible to the auditor; create and edit affordances are absent; direct navigation to an edit URL is refused by the backend.

title: admin sees both creation actions and financial fields (positive control)
objective: Help copy: "What you can see and do depends on your role..." -- control case proving the employee/auditor results are role-driven, not global breakage.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `admin`; reference data and demo assets seeded (scripts/seed-dev.sh).
test_data: The same asset used in TC-HELP-71 and TC-HELP-73.
steps: Sign in as `admin` and open the same asset detail page.
Check for financial fields and for the "New asset" action.
expected_result: Financial fields are visible and "New asset" is available in both the register header and the top bar; the create form also renders its Financial and warranty fieldset.

title: Admin-only areas are hidden and refused for non-admins
objective: Help copy: "If a page or action is hidden, the backend enforces the same restriction..." -- verify at page granularity, not just per-field.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
steps: Sign in as `employee` and inspect the sidebar for admin entries.
Navigate directly to http://localhost:3000/admin/users.
Call the corresponding admin API endpoint with the employee session.
expected_result: No admin navigation entries are rendered; direct navigation shows the 403 "Access denied" page rather than admin content; the API returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.

title: Out-of-scope asset access is refused with guidance
objective: Help copy: "...depends on your role and organizational scope... contact an administrator to request changes to your access." -- verify scope enforcement and the documented next step.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
test_data: UUID of an asset in a department outside the employee's scope (obtain as admin first).
steps: As admin, note the UUID of an asset outside the employee's department scope.
Sign in as `employee` and navigate directly to /assets/<that-uuid>.
expected_result: The asset's data is not rendered; a 403 Access denied state is shown whose message points the user to contact an administrator, matching the Help guidance; the underlying API returns 403/404 without leaking field values.

title: A forbidden register response renders a helpful alert, not a raw error
objective: Help copy: "If a page or action is hidden, the backend enforces the same restriction -- contact an administrator..." -- verify the UI translates a 403 into the documented guidance.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; signed in as `employee` (no finance.view capability, not an asset manager).
test_data: A list request forced to 403 (out-of-scope filter, or network interception).
steps: Sign in as a role whose scope yields a 403 on the asset list request (or intercept the list call and return 403 PERMISSION_DENIED).
Open http://localhost:3000/assets.
expected_result: A warning alert reads "You do not have access to these assets" with text about role or organizational scope and contacting an administrator; a correlation id is shown for support; no stack trace or raw JSON is exposed.

title: Session expiry returns the user to sign-in with a return path
objective: Help copy: "What you can see and do depends on your role..." -- verify the access boundary still holds once the session ends mid-session.
preconditions: Compose stack up; frontend reachable at http://localhost:3000; no active session.
test_data: An authenticated session whose cookie is then cleared/expired.
steps: Sign in as `admin` and open http://localhost:3000/assets with filters applied.
Clear the session cookie (or wait for expiry) and trigger a data request.
expected_result: The app redirects to /login carrying next=<the previous path> and reason=expired, and the sign-in page shows the "Your session has expired." notice; after signing in again the user returns to the original filtered URL.
